subject: humanities
passage: In ebru, the Turkish art of paper marbling, an artist sprinkles drops of pigment onto the surface of water thickened with a plant-based gum and then uses combs, brushes, or fine awls to coax the floating colors into swirling patterns. A sheet of paper laid gently on the water lifts the entire design in a single ______ result that can never be repeated exactly, since each pattern exists only until the paper takes it away.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A sheet of paper laid gently on the water lifts the entire design in a single motion" is a complete independent clause. The words that follow, "a result that can never be repeated exactly …," are a noun phrase that sums up and comments on that clause. Such a phrase is extra information and is attached to the clause with a comma.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, but "a result that can never be repeated exactly" has no main verb of its own.
explanation.B: Correct. The comma sets off the phrase "a result that can never be repeated exactly," which adds a comment on the main clause.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The period leaves "A result that can never be repeated exactly … takes it away" as a sentence fragment.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the phrase "a result that …" runs into "motion," and the sentence can't be read clearly.
